memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At the time when Amraphel was king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Kedorlaomer king of Elam and Tidal king of Goyim, these kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboyim, and the king of Bela (that is, Zoar). - Gen 14:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Suddenly Genesis reads like a news bulletin - nine kings, unfamiliar names, alliances and armies. It feels a world away from tents and altars. And that is rather the point. While Abram was quietly walking with God, the great powers of the earth were busy doing what great powers do: fighting each other for land, wealth, and dominance.

Kings rise and fall. Empires clash. Names that once made people tremble - Amraphel, Kedorlaomer - mean nothing to us now. They are footnotes in an ancient chapter. All that power, all that ambition, and history barely remembers them.

There is perspective here for us. We can be overwhelmed by the noise of world events, by the powers that seem to shape everything. But the kingdoms of this world are temporary. The headlines of every age eventually become forgotten names in old records.

Meanwhile, God's quiet work through one obedient man was building something that would outlast every one of these kingdoms. Daniel saw it clearly: "The God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed" (Dan 2:44). Don't be overawed by the powers of your day. They are passing. Invest your life in the kingdom that remains.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you more impressed by worldly power than by God's quiet work?
- What are you investing in that will outlast the kingdoms of this world?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, the kingdoms of this world rise and fall, but Your kingdom endures forever. Keep me from being overawed by passing powers. Let me invest my life in what will last.
Amen.
